apply.title: RPI Undergraduate Admissions — Apply (Application Options, Fall 2027)

test_policy.notes: "Test Optional for Fall 2027 Applicants": students may choose whether to submit SAT or ACT scores. Applicants to the Physician-Scientist (B.S./M.D.) Program must submit official scores.

requirements.notes: Fee is $70, with no fee for applications submitted by December 1 (and for Rensselaer Medalists). The general essay / personal statement satisfies RPI's essay requirement, except B.S./M.D. (reasons for a medical career) and Architecture (reasons for choosing architecture; B.Arch also needs a creative portfolio). One letter of recommendation from a counselor or teacher, preferably math or science. RPI does not conduct admissions interviews; international applicants may optionally submit an InitialView, Duolingo or Vericant interview and U.S. students an optional GLIMPSE video. FAFSA and CSS Profile are required only if seeking need-based aid (not available to most international students).

deadlines.label: Early Decision I
deadlines.notes: Binding. FAFSA/CSS Profile priority date Nov 15.

deadlines.label: Early Action
deadlines.notes: Non-binding. No application fee if submitted by Dec 1.

english_policy.waiver_notes: Non-native English speakers (or international students in U.S. colleges for under two years) must submit a test. Exemptions include SAT EBRW 640+, ACT English 22+, IB English A HL 6+, IGCSE / A-AS Level English grade B+, Cambridge B2 First or C1 Advanced score 185+, 3+ years of U.S. secondary education (request via the form on the application status page), or a diploma from a listed English-medium country. Official scores must come directly from the testing agency; self-reported scores are not accepted.

english.notes: RPI "expects a minimum" of 88 iBT; Home Edition accepted. The page gives no section minimums.
Page states 4.5 on the new 6.0 scale as the equivalent.
Overall band 6.5 in the first-year section of the page (the international-transfer section of the same page says 7.0).

aid.notes: "Limited merit scholarship opportunities" for undergraduate international students, up to $20,000 per year; all non-U.S. citizens/permanent residents must be prepared to pay the full cost of attendance. After enrolling, F-1/J-1 students must submit the International Student Financial Statement showing about one year of liquid funds (approx. $80,000 USD).
